maria (People Ops): quick one from an IC — theyre weighing a 401k loan vs hardship distribution and want to know the practical impacts (tax, match, vesting, payroll steps). tagging @kevin and @taylor for ops details :wave:
kevin (Payroll): TL;DR: loan = payroll deduction repayment, not taxed while outstanding. hardship = distribution -> taxable + maybe 10% early withdrawal penalty if <59\u00bd. vendor paperwork needed in both cases. timing matters for which pay period withholding/deduction hits.
taylor (Benefits): FYI our plan with SecurePlan supports both loans and hardship distributions but rules differ:
- Loan: generally up to 50% of vested balance (max $50k subject to IRS and plan limits). repaid via payroll deductions (post-tax principal + interest to participant). no immediate income tax if repaid on schedule.
- Hardship distribution: only allowed for certain immediate needs (medical, tuition, avoid eviction, purchase primary residence, funeral expenses). distribution is taxable and may face 10% early penalty if applicable. also reduces account balance permanently.
- Vesting: employer match already vested per schedule; a distribution doesn't "take away" already vested amounts, but reducing your balance could affect future loan amounts.
- Match: ongoing contributions still receive match. taking money out doesn't stop future matching unless contributions stop.
sasha: if they do a loan, do contributions continue? will the loan repayment reduce the contribution amount accidentally?
taylor (Benefits): Good Q. Loan repayment is a separate payroll deduction code and should not affect your elective deferral election. If someone changes their 401k contribution at the same time, that could change match. We recommend confirming both with Payroll.
kevin (Payroll): Operational checklist for employees:
1) Log into SecurePlan portal: https://portal.secureplan.example and request either "Participant Loan" or "Hardship Distribution" (paper forms accepted if preferred).
2) For loans: choose repayment term (common: 1-5 yrs; primary residence loans may have longer). SecurePlan sends approval notice with payroll deduction ID.
3) For hardship: SecurePlan issues distribution confirmation and taxable amount; they may request withholding elections.
4) Employee must forward the SecurePlan confirmation email to payroll@redwood.example with subject line: "SecurePlan 401k action  [Name]" and include employee ID by payroll cutoff.
5) Payroll needs vendor confirmation to set deduction code in the next available payroll. If you miss the cutoff, first deduction/withholding will be delayed one pay period.
6) Payroll codes we use: `SEC401K_LOAN` for loan repayments, `SEC401K_DIST` for taxable distribution amounts, `SEC401K_DIST_WHT` for tax withholding. please include the vendor reference number in the ticket.
kevin (Payroll): Note: loan repayments are post-tax deductions. For hardship, if employee elects insufficient voluntary withholding, we may still be required to withhold mandatory taxes per plan/vendor guidance. Employer match policy unchanged for ongoing contributions.
taylor (Benefits): Additional items to flag:
- Loans outstanding at termination: some plans require immediate repayment or will treat outstanding balance as a taxable distribution.
- Hardship distributions are irrevocable; you can't re-contribute that portion beyond normal deferral limits unless you do catch-up contributions within IRS rules.
- Always check SecurePlan portal for exact eligible reasons; vendor sometimes requests supporting docs (invoices, eviction notices, medical bills).
benefits-bot: Uploaded: SecurePlan quick reference (loan vs hardship) PDF  https://s3.example/secureplan-quickref.pdf
maria (People Ops): thanks both. i'll post a short FAQ blurb in #benefits-faq with the payroll codes and SecurePlan link. sasha  feel free to DM me your use-case if you want help deciding. :thumbsup:
